thread:
maria: FYI found a high-severity CVE hitting tokenizers wheels on macOS CI, looks like the new manylinux build changed a transitive dep.
vikram: Ugh, which package/version? can we short-circuit with a poetry lock pin?
maria: tokenizers 0.15.2 -> CVE-2026-1234 affects rust bindings; pip wheel pick up causes build failure in our macos-latest job. Poerty shows tokenizers being pulled by transformers 4.33.x.
elaine: Are we seeing runtime exploitability or just build-time vuln? security scan flagged it as RCE vector.
maria: Scanner flagged RCE via a deserialization path in the native lib. Must treat as high. But there is a backpatch in tokenizers 0.15.3 that fixes the patch.
jen: CI is red on a few PRs because macos wheels fail to install. Current options: 1) pin tokenizers to 0.15.3 in pyproject + poetry lock regen, 2) add a temporary pip constraint in CI, 3) branch hotfix and backport to the active release.
vikram: Also noticed our KMS key rotation tests are failing after the latest kms-client bump — unrelated but blocks staging deploy. Might be due to more strict IAM checks in kms-client 1.9.
maria: Two parallel triage threads then. For CVE: propose hotfix branch release: cherry-pick minimal change -> update pyproject.toml to add tokenizers = "^0.15.3" and run `poetry lock --no-update` to avoid other bumps.
elaine: `--no-update` will keep versions, but ensure lockfile hashes regen. We should run synth CI and smoke test embeddings route.
jen: For packaging: create branch release/hotfix/tokenizers-cve-2245, run lock regen, run tests on linux and macos runners, then push CANARY to dedicated to verify inference path.
vikram: For KMS: create a separate issue, roll back kms-client to 1.8 in staging until we validate RBAC changes. Don't mix with the CVE hotfix.
maria: Agreed. Action items: @jen create hotfix branch and draft PR, include test matrix, tag @elaine for the canary verification, @vikram to put a staging rollback PR for kms-client.
jen: I'll open PR in 10m with the lockfile diff. Will also add a CI job to run `pip install tokenizers==0.15.3` in the failing job as a stopgap if lock path fails.
ci-bot: build triggered: hotfix branch tests (macos, linux) queued.
maria: If lock regen introduces unrelated bumps, we prefer manual pin in pyproject + `poetry lock --no-update`. If that still causes pip resolver churn, fallback to a constraints file used in CI: `constraints.txt` with tokenizers==0.15.3.
elaine: Also add an audit note: record CVE id, PR link, and contact with vendor. We need to add to the security runbook for tokenizers-family.
vikram: I'll open the KMS rollback PR and tag infra-oncall. KMS rollback should be merged after hours if it affects staging only.
maria: Thanks all. Let's avoid escalations: if canary fails, we'll immediately revert and notify product. :warning:
jen: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/789 (hotfix branch, lock pin). CI greening now.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release/hotfix/tokenizers-cve-2245 -> dedicated-canary-1
maria: I'll follow canary logs. If inference latency/accuracy looks OK after the lock change, we schedule full release tomorrow morning. Otherwise revert.
vikram: KMS rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/790 — tagging infra-oncall.
elaine: Thanks team. Logging the CVE in our tracker and adding audit-log task for the KMS key policy changes.
jen: CI passed macos. Merging hotfix and cutting patch release 2.3.1-p0. :tada:
maria: Noted — please attach the lockfile diff and CVE notes to the release notes. Closing thread when releases are pushed.
